answer: Proof of Personhood serves as a vital anchor in an ocean of digital anonymity, ensuring that each wharf of the network infrastructure admits only unique human-verified actors. By requiring cryptographic challenges at the dawn of identity registration, the system forces attackers to acquire scarce biometric or social-graph validations. This imposes a significant capital expenditure, rendering the generation of thousands of automated Sybil identities economically ruinous compared to the marginal utility of protocol subversion.
